one_line: A grocery storefront where a human and AI agent collaboratively plan and manage a shared cart.
what_it_does: Co-Shop presents a grocery catalog with search, dietary/category filters, manual add controls, and an AI-assisted flow intended to plan meals under constraints while sharing the live cart with the human.
leverage_rationale: Typed WebMCP tools and shared live state are central to the claimed human-agent shopping workflow, making agent actions more reliable and visible than brittle UI-driving automation; the screenshot cannot fully verify the synchronization or checkout path.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly claims a human and AI agent share the same live cart with every action visible and editable in real time.
About text names typed tools including search_products, add_to_cart, and checkout.
Screenshot shows the AI panel beside the catalog and a WebMCP badge/agent status indicator.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent, polished prototype surface with catalog controls, product cards, prices, and an agent panel, but no video or frame sheets and no visible completed cart or checkout state. End-to-end execution is therefore only plausibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows a coherent grocery catalog with search, filters, product cards, prices, and Add controls.
Screenshot shows an AI conversation/status panel with a vegetarian dinner and budget request.
No submitted video/frame sheets; the paused media does not show completed shared-cart or checkout behavior.
impact_rationale: Grocery shoppers have a concrete, constraint-heavy planning task where agent assistance can save effort while retaining human control. The intended value is credible, though the packet does not demonstrate the complete workflow in operation.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets meal planning and grocery shopping under constraints such as budget and dietary preferences.
Screenshot visibly represents a natural-language vegetarian dinner request and grocery catalog filters.
Shared visibility/editability addresses the stated desire to avoid opaque autonomous shopping.
creativity_rationale: The human-and-agent shared-cart framing is a fresh and memorable application of WebMCP, combining natural-language planning with visible manual oversight. The grocery storefront itself is a familiar category, so novelty is primarily in the interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly centers on a jointly controlled live cart rather than an agent silently completing a purchase.
Screenshot presents the AI interaction and storefront side by side as one collaborative workspace.
About text frames WebMCP as structured, visible function calls rather than browser imitation.
usability_note: The side-by-side agent/catalog layout, visible filters, prices, and manual Add controls suggest an understandable shopping flow; cart editing, error states, and checkout usability are not shown.
red_flags: No video or frame sheets were submitted.
Static packaging screenshot does not verify live synchronization, actual WebMCP invocation, persistence, or checkout.
Access requirements and whether the demo is usable without login or an API key are unclear.
standouts: Clear WebMCP-centered use case with a human-editable shared cart.
Concrete constraint-based shopping scenario with budget and dietary needs.
Coherent visual presentation combining agent conversation and catalog controls.
advance_reason: Strong concept fit and credible visual prototype with WebMCP as a meaningful part of the intended workflow; advance despite thin execution evidence because the packet clearly communicates a differentiated collaborative shopping experience.
